title: A Generic Stack Class
oneLiner: Write a TypedStack<T> class with push, pop, peek, a count and an emptiness check, that throws the right exception when popped empty.
keyTakeaway: A generic class declares its type parameter once (class TypedStack<T>, class TypedStack[T]) and uses T for everything it stores and returns. Wrap a List<T> or a Python list, push and pop at the end for O(1), and signal misuse with the exception callers expect: InvalidOperationException in C#, IndexError in Python.
explanation:
Write a generic stack class, TypedStack, that stores items of one type T, last in, first out. It needs Push(item), Pop() which removes and returns the newest item, Peek() which returns it without removing it, Count, and IsEmpty. Popping or peeking an empty stack must throw InvalidOperationException in C#, the same as .NET's own Stack<T>. In Python the methods are push, pop, peek and is_empty, the count is len(stack) through a __len__ method, and an empty pop or peek raises IndexError, as a Python list does.

Each test runs a list of commands on a stack of ints, like ["push 3", "push 4", "pop", "peek", "count"], and reports what pop, peek, count and empty returned, with "error" when your class threw the expected exception. So that example gives [4, 3, 1, "ok"]. The final "ok" comes from a second stack, of strings, that every test pushes "ok" onto and pops: one class must work for both types.

Store the items in a List<T> (C#) or a list (Python) and push and pop at the end, where both are O(1). Count can be a property, public int Count => _items.Count, and IsEmpty another. In Python, class TypedStack[T]: (Python 3.12+) or class TypedStack(Generic[T]): states the type parameter for type checkers; the code is the same either way.

visualizationSteps.message: push 4: it goes on top, at the end of the list.
pop removes and returns the top item, 4. Removing from the end of a list is O(1).
peek returns the top item, 3, and leaves it there.
count is 1. Popping twice more would throw on the second pop: the stack would be empty.

complexity.note: Push and pop at the end of a dynamic array are O(1) (push is amortized: the occasional resize is spread over many pushes); peek, count and the empty check are O(1). The stack holds up to n items.
